text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysia's agriculture university, Universiti Pertanian is to be renamed Universiti Putra Malaysia, reflecting its shift towards a science-based institution.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad will beign a five-day official visit to Kuwait and Bahrain on Saturday to establish bilateral ties

-- Banks which have exceeded the 20 percent loan limit on higher-end property will get a grace period to bring down their exposure to the new guidelines imposed by Bank Negara. The time-frame would be negotiated on an individual basis.

-- Ting Pek Khiing, chairman of Ekran Bhd, developer of the 13.6 billion ringgit Bakun hydroelectric dam in Sarawak state, is to sue a local freelance journalist for allegedly making defamatory remarks in an Internet article which appeared on Tuesday.
-- Bank Negara's lending guidelines to the property sector and for share purchases are aimed at ensuring the economy remains on track.
